name: Count Even Numbers
description: Given an array of integers, count how many numbers are even.

explanation.idea: A number is even when dividing by 2 leaves no remainder. Check each number once and keep a tally.
explanation.analogy: Counting the red cars that pass: you look at each car once and click a counter.

steps: For each number, if num % 2 == 0 add one.

computeWithStream.summary: filter the even numbers and count them.
steps: Arrays.stream(nums) turns the array into an IntStream.
filter(num -> num % 2 == 0) keeps the even ones.
count() returns a long, so it's cast to int.
computeWithStream.spaceWhy: Streams process one element at a time; nothing is stored.

computeWithRecursion.summary: Check one index, then recurse on the rest with the running count.
steps: When index reaches the end, it returns the count.
computeWithRecursion.spaceWhy: n calls on the stack; a very large array can throw StackOverflowError.

computeWithWhile.summary: The same loop written with an explicit index.
steps: While i < length, check nums[i] and increment i.

pitfalls: Using num % 2 == 1 to test odd fails for negatives (-3 % 2 is -1 in Java). The even test == 0 is safe.
Recursion on large inputs risks StackOverflowError; Java doesn't optimise tail calls.
interview: This is a warm-up: show clean code, then mention the stream form and why recursion is a poor fit in Java.
